public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
General Galactic, a seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Halen Mattison and Luke Neise, has raised $10M to date. The sector comp universe includes one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—zero datapoints met narrow filtering criteria—rendering traditional peer-median valuation inapplicable.

Consequently, this analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $10M total raised as a proxy base value, yielding an implied valuation of $25M. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics from Seed to subsequent rounds within frontier technology sectors. The stage-progression approach is the sole applicable triangulation method given data constraints.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage peer valuation data, which limits calibration of the 2.5x multiplier to General Galactic's specific risk and market position. Validation would benefit from either identification of narrower seed-stage climate-tech peers or transaction data from the existing comp set. Until broader market pricing emerges or the company progresses to a later funding round, the $21M–$29M range carries material estimation risk.
